raw_case_text: A 61-year-old male experiencing severe dysphagia for 3 months was referred to our clinic. Computed tomography and esophagogastroduodenoscopy revealed esophageal squamous cell carcinoma with metastatic mediastinal and abdominal para-aortic lymph nodes, clinical stage IVB, cT4bN2M1, according to the Union for International Cancer Control eighth edition. Laboratory test did not reveal any abnormality except mild macrocytic anemia. To alleviate dysphagia due to malignant esophageal stenosis, the patient underwent 60 Gy of local radiotherapy in 30 fractions with concurrent chemotherapy with cisplatin 70 mg/m2 (days 1, 29) and 5-fluorouracil 700 mg/m2 (days 1-4, 29-32). Dysphagia alleviated during chemoradiotherapy; however, pancytopenia did not and it continued 6 weeks after the start of chemoradiotherapy (Fig. 1). No abnormal cells were found in the peripheral blood. Moderate fatigue and low-grade fever without respiratory symptoms developed 13 weeks after the start of chemoradiotherapy. To determine the cause of fever, computed tomography was performed 15 weeks after the start of chemoradiotherapy, which revealed diffuse ground-glass opacity in the bilateral lungs. Based on this finding combined with bronchoalveolar lavage fluid and Pneumocystis jirovecii, a diagnosis of Pneumocystis pneumonia was made. To rule out hematological malignancy, bone marrow biopsy was performed. The bone marrow smear, chromosomal test, and flow cytometry analysis indicated the development of AML. Chromosomal test revealed a complex karyotype as follows: 47, XY, add(5)(q13), add(6)(p21), add(18)(q21), -21, +marx2[13]/48, idem, +8[1]/46, idem, der(1)add(1)(p34)add(1)(q21), -add(6). Thus, a diagnosis of therapy-related AML was made by the multidisciplinary team that included hematological oncologists. The complex karyotype suggested the possibility of myelodysplastic syndrome-overt AML. Considering poor pulmonary function and the coexistence of incurable advanced esophageal cancer and unfavorable AML karyotype, the best supportive care was recommended for the patient. After consenting, the patient received the best supportive care and died 1 month after the diagnosis of therapy-related myelodysplastic syndrome-overt AML.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 61-year-old male with stage IVB esophageal squamous cell carcinoma presented 13 weeks after starting concurrent cisplatin/5-fluorouracil chemoradiotherapy with moderate fatigue, low-grade fever, and persistent pancytopenia.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Originally referred for a 3-month history of severe dysphagia and diagnosed with clinical stage IVB (cT4bN2M1) esophageal squamous cell carcinoma with mediastinal and abdominal para-aortic lymph node metastases, the patient underwent concurrent chemoradiotherapy (60 Gy in 30 fractions plus cisplatin 70 mg/m2 on days 1, 29 and 5-FU 700 mg/m2 on days 1–4, 29–32). Although his dysphagia improved, he developed persistent pancytopenia lasting beyond week 6, followed at week 13 by moderate fatigue and low-grade fever without overt respiratory symptoms.
subjective.past_medical_history: Clinical stage IVB (cT4bN2M1) esophageal squamous cell carcinoma status post concurrent 60 Gy radiotherapy and cisplatin/5-fluorouracil chemotherapy.
subjective.review_of_systems: Initial baseline positive for severe dysphagia (3 months); week 13 post-chemoradiotherapy positive for moderate fatigue and low-grade fever without respiratory symptoms.

objective.physical_examination: Low-grade fever and moderate fatigue at week 13 post-chemoradiotherapy.
objective.routine_investigations: Baseline laboratory test: Mild macrocytic anemia. Post-chemoradiotherapy hematology (week 6 onward): Persistent pancytopenia without peripheral blood blasts.
objective.advanced_workup: Chest CT (week 15 post-chemoradiotherapy): Diffuse bilateral ground-glass opacities. Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) examination: Positive for Pneumocystis jirovecii. Bone marrow aspirate/biopsy, flow cytometry, and cytogenetics: Confirmed therapy-related myelodysplastic syndrome-overt acute myeloid leukemia (t-MDS/AML) with a complex unfavorable karyotype: 47,XY,add(5)(q13),add(6)(p21),add(18)(q21),-21,+marx2[13]/48,idem,+8[1]/46,idem,der(1)add(1)(p34)add(1)(q21),-add(6).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PCP; confirmed by diffuse bilateral ground-glass opacities on chest CT and positive bronchoalveolar lavage fluid examination) and ultra-early therapy-related myelodysplastic syndrome-overt acute myeloid leukemia (t-MDS/AML with complex chromosome 5q/monosomy 21 karyotype) developing 15 weeks after concurrent cisplatin/5-FU chemoradiotherapy for stage IVB esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. Plan and clinical course: Given poor pulmonary reserve from PCP, incurable stage IVB esophageal cancer, and complex-karyotype t-AML, the multidisciplinary oncology team and patient elected best supportive care, and the patient died 1 month after the t-AML diagnosis.
